title: Impact of a tailored intervention on medication literacy for patients with oral anticancer therapy
summary:
Cancer diseases are increasingly treated with tablets. This so called “oral anticancer therapy” (OAT) has the advantage for patients that they can take their medication independently from home or on the way. Unlike with intravenous anticancer therapies, the patients no longer have to visit a practice or ambulance as often. This means that patients have to engage more with their medications. Complex therapy regimens or occurring adverse effects can be challenging. To ensure safe handling of their medicines, patients need the ability to, acquire and understand medicines information so as to determine the appropriate course of action.  This ability is referred to as ‘medication literacy’. As part of the ANIMATE project, funded by Deutsche Krebshilfe, digital educational materials are being developed to improve the medication literacy of patients with OAT. In addition, the questionnaire used to measure medication literacy is being further refined.  
To make it easier for patients to participate in the study, a user-friendly and intuitive web-based application is being developed at the beginning of the study. This guides patients digitally through the trainings and allows for easy data collection directly from home. Because the trainings are available online, the content can also be updated and adapted at any time. In this context, the patient experiences are particularly important. For this reason, supporting interviews with patients will be conducted. 
The trainings are being tested in a study involving 300 patients from several specialized oncology practices and community pharmacies. First, the medication literacy of the patients is measured using a questionnaire, which was developed as part of a preliminary project also supported by Deutsche Krebshilfe. This is how the subject areas are identified where individual support is needed. Based on the results, the patients are then offered a tailored combination of patient educations designed to specifically increase their medication literacy. The project is intended to help continuously improve the effectiveness and safety of cancer treatment with tablets.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Malignant disease ((ICD-10 C00-97-, D45-48- or E24.1-diagnosis)
- Independent intake of OAT for at least 3 months 
- Written consent to study participation
- At least one improvable area of competence in part A of the AMIKO-questionnaire
Exclusion criteria:
- Insufficient knowledge of german 
- Cognitive impairments 
(e.g. dementia)
